work.permit: Special permission of the Commissioner for Labour

note: Majority: the Age of Majority (Related Provisions) Ordinance (Cap. 410, in force 1 October 1990), section 2, a person attains full age at 18; the rules on a minor's contracts and guarantees (sections 3 and 4) are not held. Work: the Employment Ordinance (Cap. 57) defines a child as a person under 15 and a young person as 15 to 18; held as the general age, 15. The Employment of Children Regulations (Cap. 57B) bar employing a child under 13 and any child in an industrial undertaking, and let a child of 13 or 14 work in a non-industrial job with a parent's written consent, within hours limits (regulations 5 and 6) and outside the scheduled occupations, among them a place of public entertainment for profit; that 13-to-15 tier is not held. Performers: the Labour Department's Guide to the Employment of Child Entertainers says the Commissioner for Labour may permit children of different ages to be employed as entertainers by exempting them from provisions of the Regulations, on written application before the employment starts and under conditions; no age floor is set. The guide also names a notification route for some cultural performances, not held. Service: Hong Kong has no military service. That is a reading: the Basic Law, article 18, applies national laws in Hong Kong only where Annex III lists them, and the Basic Law's own list of national laws applied in Hong Kong (read 2026-10-31) holds no military service law, only the Garrison Law among defence laws.

sources.title: Hong Kong e-Legislation: Cap. 410 Age of Majority (Related Provisions) Ordinance
sources.said: (1)As from the commencement* of this Ordinance a person shall attain full age on attaining the age of 18 years. ... * Commencement date: 1 October 1990.

sources.title: Hong Kong e-Legislation: Cap. 57 Employment Ordinance, section 2
sources.said: child (兒童) means a person under the age of 15 years; ... young person (青年) means a person who has attained the age of 15 years but not the age of 18 years.

sources.title: Hong Kong e-Legislation: Cap. 57B Employment of Children Regulations
sources.said: (1)No person shall employ a child, or cause or permit a child to be employed— ... (a)who is under the age of 13 years; or ... (ii)has consented in writing to the employment.

sources.title: Labour Department, Labour Inspection Division: A Guide to the Employment of Child Entertainers
sources.said: For the development of art or training, the Commissioner for Labour may permit the employment of children of different ages as entertainers by granting exemption from certain provisions of the Employment of Children Regulations.

sources.title: The Basic Law of the HKSAR, Chapter II, article 18
sources.said: National laws shall not be applied in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region except for those listed in Annex III to this Law.
